chose: Each image's io.paulgsc.provides/requires values are literal LABEL lines at the end of its Dockerfile. A unit test in the crate that owns each edge (file_host contract.rs, orchestrator lib.rs, rust_runner lib.rs) fails unless the label equals its Rust const (CONTRACT_EPOCH, RENDER_FOLDERS_EPOCH, rust_rounds_wire::protocol::EPOCH, ws_events NATS_SUBJECTS_EPOCH).
options: Literal labels held to the consts by tests
Build-args computed in CI from the consts at build time
A build.rs or generator that writes the Dockerfile labels
gray: Build-args would make the label true by construction. But it would move the source of truth into a workflow step that CI alone runs, and a local docker build would carry wrong or no labels. Literals keep the Dockerfile readable. The cost is a second place to edit when an epoch rises, and the failing test names it.
undo: Replace the LABEL literals with ARGs fed by docker-build/docker-push and delete the three the_image_labels_are_these_epochs tests.
